subject: Metering: model-variant switches mid-session — impact on tiering and rounding
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@acmecommerce.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecommerce.com
Date: Mon, 3 Mar 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Billing question: charges when we switch models mid-conversation

Hi Hannah,

We pulled our March usage and see an unexpected jump on Mar 1 at 11:03 UTC. The spike lines up with a CI job where our agent switched from an Llama-variant to a quantized f32 model in the middle of a streaming session. It looks like both models' tokens were counted separately and pushed us into the 100k+ discount band for a single day, which then changed our tier for the month.

Can you explain how Redwood counts tokens when a single session switches model variants mid-call? Specifically:

- Are tokens billed against the model that generated them, or against the session's initial model?
- How does that interact with daily/rolling tier thresholds for discounts? We were expecting the monthly band to smooth, not flip based on a transient spike.

I attached a small CSV (acme-usage-sample.csv) with the timestamps and request ids. We're trying to reconcile before our renewal conversation next week — if this is expected behavior we may need to plan model-switch windows differently.

Thanks,
Julie
Director of AI Integrations
Acme Commerce

(attachment: acme-usage-sample.csv)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Mar 2025 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question: charges when we switch models mid-conversation

Julie — thanks for the clear log. I pulled the sample and ran it by our metering team. Short answer: tokens are attributed to the model variant that produced them, and the billing system increments banded usage atomically by token-type (generation vs embedding) on a per-day aggregation before applying monthly tiering. That can cause short spikes to move a customer into a higher monthly band if not smoothed by policy.

Longer answer and options:

- Attribution: each token is stamped with the model id at generation time. If you switch from model-A to model-B mid-session, tokens before the switch count for A, tokens after count for B. We do not retroactively reassign tokens.
- Tiering rules: monthly discounts are evaluated on a rolling monthly total but the invoice preview uses daily aggregates. A single-day burst can tip projected usage because the previewing logic is conservative.
- Rounding/minimums: we use 1-token granularity with per-call minimums of 16 tokens for streaming calls (this prevents tiny heartbeats from being billed). Those minima may have interacted with the switch if your agent sent multiple short warmup messages to the new model.

Proposals:
1) We can offer a one-time 'transition grace bucket' for Acme that would backfill the burst and prevent it from moving you into a higher tier for the March invoice. This is a manual reconciliation.
2) Long term, enable 'model-switch smoothing' on your account: when enabled, short-lived switches within a 10-minute window are attributed to the initial model for tiering purposes (not for per-token attribution). This preserves accurate per-token records but avoids tier flip-flopping.

Cc'ing Kimberly (pricing) and Ben (sales ops) to propose the concession and a small contractual tweak.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Billing
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@acmecommerce.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Mar 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question: charges when we switch models mid-conversation

Julie,

Appreciate the sample. Hannah's summary is accurate. For ACME I'd recommend the following practical approach:

- Immediate: apply a March invoice adjustment that treats the Mar 1 burst as smoothed (we'll move 60% of the burst into a non-tiered grace bucket). This is a one-time accounting credit and will be visible on your next invoice.
- Policy change: opt into model-switch smoothing (no code change required on your side). We'll enable it for your account with a note in the console.
- Discount tiers: we'll lock your current monthly tier for the remainder of the quarter if you commit to a 6% uplift on the upcoming renewal (optionally refundable as a credit if usage falls below the committed baseline).

Please confirm which option you prefer for the one-time adjustment (full credit / partial smoothing / no change). Ben will draft the amendment and update the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Pricing and Packaging
Redwood Inference

We'd like the partial smoothing option (move 60% into the grace bucket) and to opt into model-switch smoothing going forward. On the renewal lock: we need the amendment language before we commit to the uplift, but we're open to a temporary lock if you include a 30-day exit clause.

Please send the amendment and credit note so I can get procurement to sign off. Appreciated.

Best,
